paper.authors_full: Shiyingzi Huang, Lirong Long, Yanghao Zhu, Julie N.Y. Zhu
paper.title: Human–GenAI collaboration across creative phases: Cognitive mechanisms shaping novelty and usefulness
paper.pdf_filename: Huang et al (2025) - HumanGenAI collaboration across creative phases.pdf
paper.version_read: Published journal version of record: International Journal of Information Management 86 (2026), article 102986; available online 3 October 2025 (PDF p. 1).
paper.one_line_finding: Among 198 employees analyzed in Study 3, expert-rated novelty favors ChatGPT collaboration during idea generation and usefulness favors collaboration during elaboration (Table 3, p. 8: phase dummy 1 = elaboration, r = −0.30 and 0.42, respectively); the smaller Studies 2a and 2b report higher GenAI-condition novelty (6.05 vs 5.44; 42 analyzed; Table 1, p. 6) and usefulness (5.89 vs 5.49; 44 analyzed; Table 2, p. 7).

counts_source.quote: We recruited 205 full-time employees through purposive and snowball sampling. After seven participants who failed attention checks were excluded, 198 valid responses remained for analysis.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual assessment by marketing experts, using the same measurement approach as Study 2 (PDF p. 7, Section 6.2). The referenced approach uses three experts blind to purpose, hypotheses, and conditions; their average is each participant’s final score. Unless otherwise noted, the scale has seven points from strongly disagree to strongly agree (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 5.1.2). The number of raters is not separately restated for Study 3. Novelty is the innovation and uniqueness of the proposal and advertising copy (PDF p. 6, Section 5.1.2).

estimates.notes: Generation is the treatment phase because it is the proposed configuration for novelty. The printed negative correlation is preserved without changing its sign. In Table 3, the indicator codes elaboration above generation, so this correlation is oriented opposite to the named treatment/control comparison and indicates higher novelty under generation. Downstream sign handling must account for the predictor coding as well as higher_is. The novelty mediation analysis reverses the phase coding locally; its coding must not be applied to the Table 3 correlation (PDF p. 8, Sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.3). The phase contrast includes all perceived-intelligence conditions. Table 3 reports a phase-outcome correlation and significance stars, not a standardized mean difference. Its outcome means and SDs summarize the whole sample and cannot be entered as either arm’s mean or SD. No arm sizes, arm-level outcome summaries, raw phase difference, total-effect test statistic, SE, or CI are printed. The reported significance is based on participant-level expert-average scores; se_basis is participant although no numerical SE is available. The SEs and CIs in the mediation analyses are for indirect effects and are not precision estimates for this contrast. The with_ai classification concerns assistance during the ongoing proposal task. outcome_with_ai is null because access outside the assigned phase and the precise submission rated are not stated (PDF p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2; PDF p. 14, Appendices G-H); no separate unassisted transfer task is reported.

Usefulness is potential for practical implementation, solving real problems, and creating maximum value (PDF p. 6, Section 5.1.2).

estimates.notes: Elaboration is the treatment phase because it is the proposed configuration for usefulness. The positive Table 3 correlation uses elaboration above generation and therefore agrees with the named treatment/control direction. No sign transformation was applied (PDF p. 8, Sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.3). The phase contrast includes all perceived-intelligence conditions. Table 3 reports a phase-outcome correlation and significance stars, not a standardized mean difference. Its outcome means and SDs summarize the whole sample and cannot be entered as either arm’s mean or SD. No arm sizes, arm-level outcome summaries, raw phase difference, total-effect test statistic, SE, or CI are printed. The reported significance is based on participant-level expert-average scores; se_basis is participant although no numerical SE is available. The SEs and CIs in the mediation analyses are for indirect effects and are not precision estimates for this contrast. The with_ai classification concerns assistance during the ongoing proposal task. outcome_with_ai is null because access outside the assigned phase and the precise submission rated are not stated (PDF p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2; PDF p. 14, Appendices G-H); no separate unassisted transfer task is reported.

not_extracted.what: S2 / Study 2a: novelty (S2-O1) and usefulness (S2-O2), GenAI condition (idea generation phase) versus H condition (independent), and other study outcomes

not_extracted.what: S4 / Study 3: indirect effects on novelty through cognitive flexibility and on usefulness through cognitive overload
not_extracted.reason: The mediation-path estimates and their uncertainty do not measure the full-sample total contrast between assigned AI configurations. They cannot replace the phase-outcome correlation or supply its SE/CI (PDF p. 8, Section 6.3.3, Hypotheses 3 and 5).

not_extracted.what: S4 / Study 3: moderated mediation, conditional indirect effects, interactions, and simple effects involving perceived intelligence or GenAI experience
not_extracted.reason: Moderation and conditional effects are outside the requested full-sample contrast scope; the plotted simple effects additionally concern self-reported cognitive overload. No numbers were read from the figure (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 6.3.3, Hypotheses 6-7; PDF p. 9, Fig. 2).

not_extracted.what: S4 / Study 3: direct novelty and usefulness contrasts for randomized high versus low perceived GenAI intelligence
not_extracted.reason: No full-sample output contrast for this randomized factor is printed. Table 3 correlations with PGenAII concern the measured perception scale, not the randomized assignment indicator; conditional indirect effects are not total contrasts (PDF pp. 7-9, Sections 6.1-6.3 and Table 3).

not_extracted.what: S4 / Study 3: novelty/usefulness correlations with measured covariates, mediators, and each other
not_extracted.reason: These correlations do not contrast randomized AI configurations. Only the CP column represents the full-sample randomized collaboration-phase comparison (PDF p. 8, Table 3). In particular, outcome correlations with PGenAII do not identify the high-versus-low randomized intelligence manipulation.

open_items: Study 3 does not state the count randomized or any analyzed cell/phase counts. The recruitment count is not explicitly a randomization count; neither the rounded phase-indicator mean nor degrees of freedom can supply the missing counts (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1 and Table 3).

Study 3 prints no arm-level novelty/usefulness means or SDs, raw total differences, total-effect SEs/CIs, or total-effect test statistics. Table 3 prints whole-sample summaries and phase-outcome correlations only. These do not provide the codebook’s preferred within-arm standardizer (PDF p. 8, Table 3).

The novelty correlation retains the printed sign, but its predictor coding runs opposite to the named generation-versus-elaboration treatment/control comparison. Downstream orientation must explicitly reverse the predictor contrast before treating this as a treatment-minus-control effect; the extraction itself performs no transformation (PDF p. 8, Section 6.3.1 and Table 3).

The precise version of the proposal rated and ChatGPT access during the non-assigned phase are not stated. Consequently outcome_with_ai is null while question remains with_ai for phase-specific assistance on the ongoing proposal task (PDF p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2; PDF p. 14, Appendices G-H).

Preregistered primary outcomes remain unconfirmed. On 2026-10-10, urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to the paper-linked https://aspredicted.org/2hsq-9sg4.pdf and the named fallback publisher page https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0268401225001185 both failed with WinError 10013 (network socket permissions). No files were downloaded and no protocol contents were assumed (PDF p. 7, Section 6.1).

The underlying ChatGPT model/version and study-specific prompts are not given. The recorded tool year is the ChatGPT product release year explicitly stated in the introduction (PDF p. 1, Section 1; PDF p. 7, Section 6.1).

The participant country is not stated. The paper describes most participants as based in East Asia, which does not identify a country or a Study 3-specific country distribution (PDF p. 10, Section 7.3).

Study 3 prints no full-sample novelty/usefulness contrast of randomized high versus low perceived GenAI intelligence. Table 3 PGenAII is the measured perception scale, not the assignment dummy. Factorial-cell summaries or author analysis outputs would be needed for this additional contrast (PDF pp. 7-9, Sections 6.1-6.3 and Table 3).
